title: Workload Identity Lab
summary: Federated agents: authenticate to the gateway with a JWT from your own identity platform — no gateway secret. Signature, issuer, audience, required claims; Pass Agent Token passthrough.

cards.title: What workload identity is
cards.body: An agent identifies with a JWT its own platform issued (PF, K8s, GitHub Actions, any OIDC). The gateway trusts the issuer cryptographically instead of holding a secret for the agent.

cards.title: The gateway's check chain
cards.body: Signature against the registered JWKS, then exact issuer, exact audience, required claims (act.sub, client_id), token lifetime. Any failure is 401 with the stage named.

cards.title: Pass Agent Token
cards.body: The gateway forwards the caller's workload token to the backend unchanged, so the backend verifies the same federated identity. Only callers that came in with a workload assertion can use apps on this mode.

cards.title: Virtual key vs workload identity
cards.body: Virtual key: a secret the gateway issued and looks up. Workload identity: a JWT the caller's platform issued and the gateway verifies. Same grant/policy machinery; different trust direction.

cards.title: Break it on purpose
cards.body: Flip a signature char (401 signature). Wrong audience — what happens when the default token manager answers (401 audience). The stage named in the refusal is the teaching point.
